Title: Senior Citizens Bill to strengthen protection for elderly, says Nancy Shukri
Article:
MELAKA: The physical and mental well-being of senior citizens will be among the key areas addressed under the Senior Citizens Bill, which is expected to be tabled in the cabinet soon, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said the bill was being drafted to ensure senior citizens receive adequate protection and enjoy a better quality of life.
"The government already has policies and frameworks in place for senior citizens, and this bill is a follow-up measure to further strengthen their protection.
"The bill specifically focuses on safeguarding senior citizens so that they are protected in all aspects," she told reporters after officiating the 2026 National-Level Senior Citizens Day celebration at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here today.
Also present was Social Welfare Department director-general Datuk Che Murad Sayang Ramjan.
Nancy said the bill reflected the government's commitment to strengthening support, protection and care systems for senior citizens, ensuring they remain relevant to current needs and future demographic changes.
She added that senior citizens should not be regarded as a burden, but valued and encouraged to serve as role models for younger generations as part of efforts to strengthen family values.
On independent motivational speakers, Nancy said her ministry was ready to work with relevant parties to screen individuals appointed to deliver talks and ensure they had the necessary qualifications and were of the requisite calibre.
"It would not be entirely appropriate for us to take over the responsibility (of conducting the screenings) as the matter comes under the purview of other agencies or ministries. However, we can work together by reminding those organising such talks to ensure that the speakers are of the requisite calibre," she said.
Police received a report on Sept 26 alleging that a motivational speaker had sexually harassed a child.
Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was lodged at 2.09am and the case was being investigated under Section 12 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. – BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Boy survives five-hour surgery after brutal stray dog attack
Article:
BACHOK: An 8-year-old boy underwent five-hour surgery after he was seriously injured in an attack by five stray dogs at Pantai Kuala Kemasin here last Thursday.
The victim, Azuar Firdaus Zuraiman, underwent surgery to clean and close the bite wounds, including puncture marks from the dogs' teeth on his head and neck.
His father, Zuraiman Mahmod, 47, said his eighth child of nine siblings was playing at the beach with several relatives at about 9am when the incident occurred.
He said a group of stray dogs suddenly approached and chased them, causing his son to fall before the animals attacked and bit him.
"My son managed to get up and kick the animals before running towards the water, which was when the dogs stopped attacking him.
"The incident was noticed by a worker who happened to be in the area. He brought my son to our food stall near the beach," he said when contacted today.
Zuraiman said he had been running a food business in the area for years and the latest incident was the second stray dog attack there in two years.
He said a fisherman had previously injured his hand after being attacked by stray dogs, adding that he never expected one of his children to become a victim.
He said his son underwent surgery from 1pm to 5pm yesterday and was now in stable condition while receiving treatment at Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II (HRPZII) in Kota Bharu.
Zuraiman said stray dogs had been a longstanding problem in the area and residents had previously lodged complaints.
Meanwhile, Bachok district police chief Superintendent Mohamad Ismail Jamaluddin confirmed receiving a report on the incident.
He said further investigations were underway.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar attends F1 qualifying, inspects Sepang preparations
Article:
SEPANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today attended the Formula One (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix qualifying session at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), where he also inspected preparations for the race.
Anwar arrived at the circuit at 4.50pm and was received by Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Petronas president and group chief executive officer Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik, SIC chairman Datin Anita Azrina Abdul Aziz and other dignitaries.
He then toured the Mercedes-AMG Petronas team pit for about 15 minutes.
Following the session, Anwar attended a welcome dinner hosted by Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al-Khalifa at the paddock.
The F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia began yesterday with the first and second free practice sessions, followed by the third free practice session and qualifying today.
The 56-lap race is scheduled to start at 3pm tomorrow.
The event marks the return of Formula One to Sepang after a 9-year absence, with the circuit last hosting an F1 race in 2017.
In July, Formula 1 and the International Automobile Federation (FIA) confirmed that Malaysia would host the F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement involving F1, the FIA and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The arrangement enables the Bahrain Grand Prix to remain on the 2026 F1 calendar after the original event could not proceed in Bahrain, with the race relocated to Sepang amid the situation in West Asia.
The return of Formula One to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and King Hamad bin Isa Al-Khalifa of Bahrain, as well as the two governments.
Formula One made its debut at Sepang in 1999, with the circuit hosting the Malaysian Grand Prix until 2017.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Soldier held after pistol, ammunition and suspected ketum found at army camp
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A soldier was arrested after he was found with a pistol, dozens of rounds of ammunition and a liquid suspected to be ketum at the parking area of an army camp here on Tuesday.
Cheras deputy police chief Superintendent Lim Chun How said the man, in his 30s, was arrested by a team from the Cheras district police headquarters' Crime Prevention and Community Safety Division at 12.42am.
"Checks found that the soldier had three previous criminal records involving two drug-related cases and one criminal case," he said in a statement this afternoon.
He said the soldier was initially remanded for five days to facilitate investigations under Section 8 of the Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971 and Section 8(a) of the Arms Act 1960.
"The suspect's remand period ended today but was extended by another five days until Oct 8," he said.

Title: Tengku Zafrul: Malaysia has shifted from efficiency to resilience amid global uncertainty
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economic focus has shifted from pursuing efficiency to building greater resilience as the country continues to outperform growth forecasts despite global uncertainty.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz said economic leadership also meant preparing Malaysia to seize clear opportunities while remaining resilient to unpredictable shocks.
He said key fiscal reforms, including fuel subsidy rationalisation and the Fiscal Responsibility Act, had strengthened Malaysia's public finances.
"But economic reform must be matched by compassion; we must safeguard the vulnerable while building national capacity.
"We must proactively lift incomes by ensuring wages rise alongside productivity, creating higher-paying jobs and boosting entrepreneurship," he said in his special leadership address at the Youth Economic Forum.
The former investment, trade and industry minister said trade routes were being redrawn while artificial intelligence was both empowering and disrupting the workforce, reshaping jobs that had once provided young people with their first foothold in a career.
Tengku Zafrul said Malaysia's young population could become an economic dividend only if it translated into higher productivity, innovation, high-value jobs and new businesses.
"As record investment flows into our region and our country, we must keep asking: what does this investment create for Malaysians? How many high-income jobs? How many young engineers with new skills? How many small and medium-sized enterprises plugged into global supply chains?
"Capital should build stronger firms, and technology should build better skills," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lee's resignation a wake-up call for PKR, says Selangor party strategist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The resignation of Petaling Jaya member of parliament Lee Chean Chung should serve as a wake-up call for PKR to strengthen its organisation, improve communication and better manage differences within the party, said Selangor PKR strategy director Mohd Yahya Mat Sahri.
However, he said Lee's departure should not be viewed as a failure of the Madani government or Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
"This should serve as a wake-up call to the entire PKR family to strengthen organisational discipline, improve communication, manage differences of opinion better and ensure the reform agenda remains the party and government's pulse," he said.
Yahya said Lee's resignation, along with the departure of other PKR MPs, should not automatically be interpreted as meaning the Madani government had lost its majority or the people's mandate.
"The government's position is determined by majority support in the Dewan Rakyat, while the people's overall mandate will continue to be determined through the democratic process and elections.
"Therefore, any claim that the Madani government has lost its mandate based solely on this development is a premature conclusion," he said.
He said criticism of the government should not be feared, but allegations concerning weaknesses in administration, governance or policy should be addressed with facts.
Yahya said PKR should ensure internal differences did not develop into wider divisions, adding that party members should be given space to express their views while respecting decisions reached through the party's internal democratic processes.
He also urged Anwar to remain focused on the government's broader priorities, including the economy, cost of living, employment, institutional reform, governance, investment, education and public welfare.
"Political differences within a party can happen, but we must not allow differences within the party to become a distraction to the stability of the government and the interests of the people," he said.
Lee, who was suspended by PKR for three years on Sept 30, announced his resignation as Petaling Jaya MP effective Oct 2. He said he would submit his formal letter to leave PKR on Oct 5.
His resignation makes him the fourth PKR MP to leave the party this year, following former deputy president Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli and former vice-president Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad in May, and Wong Chen in August.
Rafizi and Nik Nazmi vacated their Pandan and Setiawangsa seats before taking over Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
Rafizi described the move as a political reset and said they wanted a new platform free from the existing parties' political calculations.
Wong Chen subsequently resigned as Subang MP and left PKR before joining Bersama. He said dissatisfaction with the pace of the Madani government's reform agenda was a key factor in his decision.
Lee had previously resigned from PKR's Central Leadership Council in June but said at the time that he would remain in the party and continue serving as Petaling Jaya MP.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'It starts at home': Fadhlina calls on families to lead Malaysia's reading push
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A vibrant reading culture must begin at home before extending to schools and the wider community to build an intellectual society, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said.
She said fostering long-term literacy required a concerted effort involving families, schools and government-led initiatives.
She cited national programmes including student book vouchers and the Kota Buku project, which are aimed at ensuring access to quality literature for all children.
Fadhlina said reading should go beyond basic academic requirements to encourage deeper critical thinking, courtesy and comprehension.
"We also require deep reading — meaning understanding every page and character with a stronger message," she said on the sidelines of the National Seminar: Works and Thoughts of Lim Swee Tin today.
Highlighting the role of women in shaping reading habits at home, Fadhlina said initiatives such as the Kelab Perempuan Membaca (Women's Reading Club) could help strengthen reading culture among families.
"Between the strengths of reading, as I mentioned, it begins at home, and we give focus to mothers," she said, adding that such platforms provided essential support networks for families.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Brunei Sultan, Prince Mateen touch down in Subang for Sepang F1 race
Article:
SUBANG: Sultan of Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah arrived in Malaysia today for a special visit in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
The special aircraft carrying His Majesty and the Brunei delegation, including Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, landed at the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base here at 4.28pm.
They were welcomed by Tunku Temenggong Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Al-Haj Sultan Ibrahim and Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari.
His Majesty then inspected a guard of honour comprising 2 officers and 26 personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Malay Regiment, led by Captain Wan Amirul Syafiq Wan Zamri.
SIC has been selected to host the 2026 F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP, making the iconic circuit a temporary venue for the prestigious race, which began yesterday and runs until Sunday.
Last July, Formula 1 confirmed that Malaysia would host the race following an agreement between Formula 1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement ensured the Bahrain GP remained on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian GP at Sepang from 1999 to 2017 before it was dropped from the F1 calendar.
The return of the race to Malaysia follows diplomatic efforts involving His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and King Hamad Isa Al-Khalifa of Bahrain.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Master AI or AI will master us, Anwar tells youth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian youth must master emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), to ensure the country keeps pace with rapid global change, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said mastering new technologies could reshape the way young people think, live and participate in the economy of the future.
"When it comes to AI, you are probably more knowledgeable than I am. I do not have to ask because I know my own understanding is limited.
"But what I want to stress, as a father, is that we must uphold our values. At an international forum in Shanghai recently with the Chinese premier, I said that we must master AI.
"If we do not, AI will master us. So, we must give our young people the space to seriously master this knowledge," he said at the 2026 Youth Economic Forum at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre today.
Anwar said a new generation equipped with knowledge, discipline and strong values could help propel Malaysia towards greater progress.
"Imagine if those here today, representing the present and future generations, possess a new awareness, refuse to compromise, maintain strong discipline and have firm determination — not only for yourselves, but also for your families, children and the future.
"Then we will have a generation whose mindset and thinking are different from outdated ways of thinking — that corruption is acceptable, stealing is acceptable, oppression is acceptable and keeping people ignorant is acceptable.
"No. This is a new generation, with a new resolve," he added.
Anwar said he was confident that a renewed spirit among young people could propel Malaysia forward rapidly, with the country becoming more progressive and successful within the next decade.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar recalls childhood lesson on stealing, tells youths to reject corruption
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today drew on a childhood lesson about stealing to remind the younger generation to reject corruption and leaders who abuse their positions for personal gain.
Anwar said young people should retain their idealism and refuse to tolerate corruption.
He said the lesson had been instilled in him when he was 8 or 9 years old, after he took four nutmegs from an orchard in Cherok Tok Kun near Bukit Mertajam, Penang, without the owner's permission.
Anwar said his grandmother questioned him after he returned home with the fruits and told him that taking something without permission amounted to stealing.
"My grandmother said, 'Anwar, if you take something without permission from anyone, even four nutmegs, that is stealing. And stealing is a sin,'" he said in his speech at the 2026 National Youth Economic Forum.
Despite it being close to nightfall, Anwar said his grandmother insisted that he return the nutmegs immediately.
Anwar recalled running back to the orchard and throwing the four nutmegs onto the property before returning home, saying he did not understand then why his grandmother had been so strict over something seemingly small.
"But that taught me, when I became Prime Minister, do not steal and do not allow people to steal," he said.
Anwar said some might accuse him of using a gathering of young people to talk politics, but rejected the suggestion that youths were incapable of thinking for themselves.
"You think these young people are stupid? These are intelligent young people, the best of the best. They can think, they know.
"At school, if you steal a pencil, the teacher gets angry. You steal a pencil or pen, you get scolded. But when a leader steals billions of ringgit, that is okay?
"What knowledge is that? What manners? What morals are we learning?" he said.
Anwar urged young Malaysians to support those who upheld integrity and reject leaders involved in corruption or abuse of power, saying wrongdoing should not be excused.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 690 terrapin hatchlings released into Sungai Kemaman to boost conservation
Article:
CHUKAI: Some 690 terrapin hatchlings were released into their natural habitat in Sungai Kemaman near Kampung Pasir Gajah here today.
Turtle Conservation Society of Malaysia (TCS) co-founder and executive director Dr Chen Pelf Nyok said the terrapin eggs were incubated for three months, after which the hatchlings were temporarily cared for at the Terrapin Conservation Centre in Kampung Pasir Gajah.
She said TCS had collected more than 1,600 terrapin eggs this year, with over 1,200 successfully hatching.
Chen said the terrapin hatchlings were released in stages, with today's release marking the completion of this year's programme.
"I hope the terrapins released today will reach maturity and eventually return to the river to lay eggs," she said when met during the programme here today.
Last year, 680 terrapin hatchlings were released into the river.
Chen hoped the programme would encourage local residents to develop a greater appreciation for the wildlife in their area, while visitors could help raise awareness about terrapin conservation through social media.
"Through this programme, more people can learn about terrapins and support conservation efforts to protect this increasingly threatened species," she said.
Chen said that besides Sungai Kemaman, terrapins were also found in the Terengganu and Dungun rivers, where conservation efforts were carried out by the State Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan).
Meanwhile, visitor Noor Hayati Mamat, 35, said she was excited to have the opportunity to hold and release a terrapin hatchling for the first time.
"This experience not only gives visitors the opportunity to learn more about terrapins, but also instils a shared sense of responsibility to protect their natural habitat," she said.
Another visitor, Hanafiah Harun, 48, said the programme brought the community closer to wildlife conservation efforts while providing first-hand exposure to the importance of protecting terrapins.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Don't make us second victims': Nepal flood families demand central bank debt relief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Families of the 54 Malaysians still unaccounted for after the Nepal flash floods and landslides have welcomed Bank Negara Malaysia's (BNM) readiness to facilitate financial assistance, but want a single, centrally coordinated framework.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said BNM's indication that financial institutions may consider repayment deferments, fee and charge waivers, documentation flexibility and expedited insurance and takaful claims was a positive step.
"Given the unprecedented nature of this tragedy, we respectfully believe the next step should be a BNM-driven, centrally coordinated framework, rather than requiring 54 families to navigate different banks, insurers and financial institutions individually," he said in a statement.
"We do not want 54 families to be required to navigate potentially hundreds of separate administrative processes across multiple financial institutions and service providers.
"Most importantly, the next of kin must not become the second victims of this tragedy," he added.
Manivannan said BNM's move was welcome after what the families described as 39 days of uncertainty, anguish and unanswered questions.
He said the families wanted a temporary moratorium or repayment deferment, without interest, profit or late payment charges, on liabilities registered in the names of the missing persons.
These include housing, vehicle and personal financing, credit facilities and overdrafts.
He stressed that the request did not cover the personal liabilities of next of kin or other family members.
For vehicle financing, he called for a clear mechanism, including voluntary surrender where continued payments were no longer sustainable, without the next of kin being treated as the borrower.
Any surplus from a sale should be released to the person or estate legally entitled to it, he said.
He also called for a lawful mechanism to identify, preserve and protect the missing persons' assets, including bank deposits, shares, unit trusts, Employees Provident Fund (EPF) savings, e-wallets, and insurance and takaful policies.
"Families should not be expected to independently identify every bank, financial institution, investment platform, insurer, takaful operator or other provider with which a missing person may have an account, investment, policy or financial interest," Manivannan said.
He said the families had requested a meeting with BNM next week through BNMLINK and Offices Department (JLPB) deputy director Hasjun Hashim, and asked that the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) also take part.
The A-GC's involvement, he added, would ensure the proposed measures were considered within the appropriate legal framework, given that there was no confirmed death or other formal legal status.
Manivannan said the families were not seeking to have debts written off.
"We are asking for breathing space, clarity, protection of their loved ones' assets, and a fair and humane mechanism while the legal status of their loved ones remains unresolved," he added.
Masfih also renewed its plea for a meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, which it said it had repeatedly sought since the early days of the tragedy.
"The families are not asking for special treatment. They are asking for clarity, coordination, protection and continued government support while they wait for their loved ones," Manivannan said.
Previously, 55 Malaysians were listed as uncontactable after flash floods and landslides struck Rasuwa District in Nepal on Aug 26. The floods also affected areas along the Nepal-Tibet border.
Yesterday,
one of the 55 Malaysians
was reportedly found safe and returned home, according to MASFIH.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 77-year-old man feared drowned was due to remarry in December [WATCH]
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: A 77-year-old man who was feared drowned after his car plunged into a river in Lubuk Kawah last night was supposed to remarry on Dec 12.
Mat Yusof Hashim was believed to have been on his way home to Jalan Masjid, Felda Teloi Timur, after dropping off his future wife in Sidam following dinner together.
His son, Muhamad Noor, 43, said the family had accepted the incident and was hoping his father would be found soon.
"My father was supposed to get married on Dec 12.
"We have accepted what has happened and can only hope that he will be found soon," he said when met at the scene today.
The couple had been making preparations for their marriage for the past two months.
"My mother died in December last year and my father had been living alone ever since. He wanted to remarry the woman he had chosen to spend the rest of his life with.
"But when I received news that my father was
missing
about 2am, I immediately came here with my brother, hoping that he would be found soon," he said.
Meanwhile, Mat Yusof's future wife, Nisun Che Mat, 69, said he had picked her up in Sidam after Asar prayers yesterday to have dinner and discuss their wedding plans.
"Throughout the time we were together until last night, he seemed happy and spoke normally.
"He told me he would come to pick me up this Monday as I needed to have a blood test at the hospital as part of the marriage registration process, and I agreed," she said.
Nisun said she hoped Mat Yusof would be found as soon as possible.
It was reported that Mat Yusof was
feared drowned
after the car he was driving plunged into a river last night.
A search and rescue operation is underway at the scene, but no leads have been found so far.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Doctor loses RM300,000 in fake student investment scheme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A private medical practitioner lost RM300,000 after falling victim to an investment scam involving a non-existent Kad Prihatin Siswa project.
Ampang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said the victim, a 38-year-old local woman, and her husband began dealing with a male suspect over the purported project in early 2023.
He said they dealt with the suspect face-to-face and via WhatsApp in Lembah Jaya Utara.
"The suspect introduced the project as an investment scheme purportedly involving 20 universities and about 620,000 students.
"He also promised lucrative returns to investors. Enticed by the offer, the victim made 5 transactions totalling RM300,000 into a bank account belonging to the suspect throughout 2023," he said in a statement today.
Khairul Anuar said an investment agreement was subsequently signed between the victim and the suspect, promising returns of 10 per cent a month for 12 months.
Under the agreement, the victim was also promised the return of her capital at the end of the investment period and was registered as a 10 per cent shareholder in the company.
"However, the promised profits and dividends have never been received by the victim to this day.
"The victim and her husband repeatedly sought explanations, demanded payment of the dividends and requested a copy of the stamped agreement, but the suspect gave various excuses and failed to provide a solution," he said.
Realising she had been duped, the victim lodged a police report.
Khairul Anuar said police were investigating the case and no arrests had been made so far.
"The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating and dishonestly inducing the delivery of property.
"Upon conviction, the offence carries a jail term of between 1 and 10 years, whipping and a possible fine," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bahrain F1 Grand Prix: Spectators complain about expensive food, drinks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Food and beverage prices at Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) have sparked discussion online after several spectators shared their experiences on social media.
Among the prices that went viral were RM50 for turmeric chicken rice, RM30 for mango with asam boi, RM25 for iced Milo and RM25 for fruit drinks.
A Threads user, @myk3_mash, also questioned the alleged RM50 price of Chinese fried rice.
"How can Chinese fried rice be sold for RM50? I swear I bought this for RM7 at a mamak restaurant yesterday," the user said in a post.
The prices prompted various reactions, with some netizens joking that the cost of food had discouraged them from attending the race.
"No wonder I didn't feel like going to the F1. We're clearly not the target audience. I can't afford it," said user @daripadakeme.gifts.
Others, however, suggested that the prices could be attributed to high operating costs and vendor site rental fees at the event venue.
One social media user, @mudayat98, claimed that renting a vendor site for three days could cost RM30,000, with some sites allegedly costing over RM100,000.
"The prices are like that because renting a site for three days costs RM30,000, and some are even over RM100,000.
"If you want it cheap, just watch the F1 on television and then buy food at the night market," the user said.
The user also claimed that the F1 organisers took about 20 per cent of sales revenue.
"Even RM25 is considered cheap. Besides that, the F1 organisers also take about 20 per cent of the sales revenue, if I'm not mistaken," the user added.
The posts have since sparked wider discussion among netizens about food prices at major events, particularly the difference between prices charged within event venues and those outside.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Maintenance worker dies after being electrocuted while repairing house roof
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: A man died after he was believed to have been electrocuted while repairing the roof of a terrace house in Taman Berangan here this morning.
Cheng Gwo Pyng, 49, a maintenance worker, became unconscious after being electrocuted while on the roof of the house.
The victim was rushed to hospital but was pronounced dead while receiving treatment.
It is understood that the victim had gone to the house to replace an electrical box for a customer before the incident.
Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan confirmed the incident and said the case had been classified as sudden death.
"Police received a report on the incident about 11.35am today," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH to announce Melaka election candidates within 2 weeks, says Amirudin
Article:
KLANG: Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka election within the next two weeks, said PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said PH had been preparing for the 16th Melaka election for about two months, including meetings with its election machinery and teams.
"Preparations have been ongoing for the past two months, including meetings with our election machinery and teams.
"I believe the PH machinery is already moving and ready. The only matter is the alignment and understanding with other parties, which is still being worked out.
"We only need to announce the candidates. God willing, in the near future, within a week or two, we will announce our candidates," he said.
He said this after officiating the launch of the RM1,500 benefits handover programme for Tawas members at the KSL Convention Centre here today.
Amirudin said PH remained open to discussions if there was still room for negotiations with other parties.
"If not, we are also prepared to contest based on our existing capabilities and understanding.
"We are looking at the possibilities. Perhaps next week, or within a week or two, we will have a clearer picture. Sometimes, this is how political parties operate," he said.
He said the current political landscape was fluid, with parties seeking the best solutions and partners to achieve the best outcome in the election.
"So, this process of trying and testing is happening among the parties. Some have succeeded, while others have not.
"But we will continue to offer the people what we can, based on what we have proven in the state and the achievements we have made," he said.
However, Amirudin declined to comment further when asked about Pas' position on forming an alliance with Barisan Nasional (BN).
"Yesterday, they said it was 90 per cent, with 10 per cent remaining. Anything can happen.
"I do not want to interfere in their affairs. Let them make their own decision," he said.
Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh previously announced that the Melaka Legislative Assembly was dissolved effective Sept 23, paving the way for the 16th Melaka election.
The dissolution was consented to by Yang di-Pertua Negeri Melaka Tun Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar hints 2027 Budget will address financial hardship among university students [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hinted that the 2027 Budget will include measures to address financial hardship among university students, including those struggling with hunger and debt.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the unity government had always listened to the aspirations and concerns of youths, particularly those pursuing higher education.
"There are university students who say, 'We want to study, but we are hungry.' We are focusing on that. I will announce it during the Budget.
"There are poor students who cannot afford it and are forced to take on debt. These are things we have to listen to and address," he said in his speech at the National Youth Economic Forum at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here today.
Anwar did not disclose details of the measures being considered, saying further announcements would be made when the 2027 Budget is tabled, scheduled for Oct 9.
He said the government had a responsibility to provide young Malaysians with opportunities to pursue education and prepare themselves for emerging fields.
He also said young Malaysians should not be regarded merely as future leaders, saying he had long disliked politicians describing youths as the country's "leaders of the future" when they should already be involved in helping to lead the nation.
"I don't like hearing that because the statement is misleading. Young people today, in the current narrative, are of course the leaders of the future, but young people today must also help and lead the country.
"You are not only leaders of the future, but also leaders now, working together," he said.
Anwar said this required young people to look beyond their own associations, regions, ethnic groups or religious perspectives and think within the broader framework of safeguarding the country and strengthening national unity.
He added that young people should not be reduced to political tools expected to follow blindly, or have their freedom to think, speak and question suppressed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Bandar Utama schoolgirl's family sues govt, others over her death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The mother and sister of Yap Shing Xuen, who was killed on Oct 14 last year, have filed a civil suit in the Kuala Lumpur High Court against several parties over her death.
In a statement, the mother said the suit, filed on Oct 1 through Messrs Surendra Ananth, named several government agencies, the parents of the boy who killed Yap and the boy himself as defendants.
She said the family believed Yap's death could have been prevented had the relevant parties taken appropriate steps, particularly in addressing mental health issues among students.
"This is not about vengeance. It is about ensuring that the relevant parties are held accountable so that this does not happen to any other child," she said.
She claimed that the government agencies named as defendants had failed to take adequate preventive measures to address mental health issues in schools before matters escalated.
The mother also said the suit named the boy's parents as defendants, claiming that there had been warning signs and that parents had a responsibility to ensure their children did not harm others.
The boy was also named as a defendant in the suit.
"These are very important issues. There should be a full trial so that all these issues can be properly heard and examined by the court," she said.
The mother said the case also highlighted the need for proper implementation of policies concerning mental health among schoolchildren.
"With the increasing mental health challenges faced by our children today, we cannot choose to stay silent anymore. Grand statements and plans are insufficient. We cannot wait until more lives are lost before proper action is taken," she said.
She said Yap had gone to school on Oct 14, 2025, expecting her to return home as usual.
"But on that day, I lost a daughter, and my eldest daughter lost her sister.
"No mother or sister should ever have to go through what we did. We want the relevant parties to be held accountable," she said.
The family's legal team will be led primarily by Datuk Malik Imtiaz and Surendra Ananth.
The family said media enquiries regarding the civil suit should be directed to its lawyers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bahrain F1 Grand Prix: Spectators told not to cut queues
Article:
SEPANG: Spectators attending the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and road users around the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here should follow the instructions of police on duty to ensure smooth movement in and out of the venue.
KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M Ravi said police and all relevant parties had made thorough preparations to ensure the main event tomorrow ran smoothly.
"Today, the organiser has added more buses and personnel to manage the crowds.
"When many people leave and are concentrated in one area, congestion will inevitably occur.
"So I urge the public to be patient, respectful and cooperate with the officers on duty, and not to cut the queue," he said when contacted.
He said road users around SIC were also asked to cooperate and comply with the diversions and road closures implemented in the area to ease traffic flow.
It was previously
reported
that fans' excitement at watching the grand prix at SIC turned into a nightmare when they had to wait for hours and scramble to board shuttle buses home after the first day ended yesterday.
Some fans even walked nearly 18km because they could not bear waiting in the congestion and scrambling for the buses provided to take them out of the circuit area.
Meanwhile, the movement of visitors was described as more orderly this morning compared with yesterday, particularly in terms of queues and shuttle bus services.
Checks on social media found that several users praised the marshals and security guards for ensuring spectators queued properly and stopping attempts to cut the queue.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Financial institutions ready to assist families of Nepal flood victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Financial service providers stand ready to extend appropriate relief and support to the families of victims affected by the recent floods along the Nepal-China border, in line with applicable laws and regulatory requirements, said Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM).
The central bank said assistance or goodwill measures could include repayment deferments, waivers of fees and charges, and flexibility in documentation requirements pending completion of the relevant legal processes.
"Financial institutions may also prioritise the processing and validation of policy or certificate status, expedite the payment of insurance and takaful claims, and provide other forms of support tailored to the specific needs of the affected families," BNM said in a statement.
BNM advised the next of kin of affected Malaysians to reach out to the relevant financial institutions for appropriate assistance.
The central bank said it would work closely with financial institutions to ensure the timely provision of support to those affected by the tragedy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Replacing cancelled Norway missiles could cost Malaysia over RM1bil
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Procuring a new surface-to-surface missile system after Malaysia's Naval Strike Missile (NSM) deal with Norway was cancelled could cost the government more than RM1 billion.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said fresh funding was needed for replacement missiles as the navy's warships could not be left without a primary missile system.
He said the Norwegian government had refused to advance a refund for payments already made by Malaysia, forcing the Defence Ministry to consider suppliers from three other countries.
The cost is estimated at between RM700 million and more than RM1 billion.
"It is not easy. First, the Norwegian government itself has washed its hands of the matter, even though it is the source of the problem.
"Even though we said it would demonstrate the long-standing friendship between the two countries and signal our desire to maintain those ties, what is wrong with them advancing what we have
already paid
? But they refused.
"So, with the Norwegian government, we should not expect anything, and as for the company, they are trying to delay and so on."
He said these were among the challenges faced by Malaysia.
"Our money is stuck there, and we will continue to pursue the claim. The question is how we replace the missiles meant for those ships.
"That is why the government may need to consider providing a new allocation to purchase new missiles to replace those from Norway," he told a press conference after the ground-breaking ceremony for the Kota Tinggi Islamic Orphanage Hostel.
On the criteria for replacing the NSM system, Khaled said several factors beyond price were being evaluated.
He said delivery timelines and technological compatibility with the existing Combat Management System (CMS) on the ships were among the ministry's top priorities.
"Missiles are not like buying cars at a showroom where you can drive them off immediately. Ordering them takes three to four years.
"Second, can it integrate with the weapon system and the CMS on the ship?
"The CMS on the ship comes from France's Naval Group.
"So, whatever missile we choose to buy, can it integrate with that system? We must consider all these aspects alongside price," he added.
In July, it was
reported
that Norway had unilaterally revoked the export licence without prior notice, informing Malaysia only when delivery of the missiles was due.
Oslo had said that it would export the missile system only to Nato members and allied countries, with no further explanation despite repeated requests from Malaysia.
For the record, the Putrajaya had already paid nearly 95 per cent of the total contract value, amounting to more than RM500 million.

Title: MAF to rebalance personnel deployment between peninsula, Sabah and Sarawak
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: The government will restructure the deployment of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak to ensure a more balanced concentration of defence assets, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
He said the government was targeting an even split, with 50 per cent of MAF personnel stationed in the peninsula and the remaining 50 per cent in Sabah and Sarawak.
Currently, about two-thirds of MAF personnel are deployed in the peninsula, while the remaining one-third are stationed in Sabah and Sarawak, totalling about 20,000 personnel at any given time.
"We want the ratio to be 50 per cent each in the peninsula and in Sabah and Sarawak, to balance it out," he told reporters after the groundbreaking ceremony for the Asrama Anak-Anak Yatim Islam Kota Tinggi here today.
On military activities on Balabac Island in the Philippines, located near Malaysia, Khaled said the matter should be viewed from the perspective of preparedness rather than as a direct threat to the country.
"I want to clarify that we are not worried about the military build-up in Balabac. What I want to emphasise is that when the Philippines upgrades its bases and military presence there, any dispute or clash in that geopolitically small area could spill over into Malaysia," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drunk motorcyclist crashes into 2 marathon runners in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A motorcyclist who allegedly rode through a road closure before travelling against traffic crashed into two Standard Chartered Kuala Lumpur Marathon (SCKLM) 2026 participants early today.
The 21-year-old rider subsequently tested positive for alcohol in a preliminary breath test, recording an Evidential Breath Analyser (EBA) reading of 164mg/100ml.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the incident occurred at Jalan Munshi Abdullah about 6.15am.
"Preliminary investigations found that the rider, who was carrying a 19-year-old pillion passenger, had passed through a section of road closed off with traffic cones.
"The rider was ordered to stop by a police officer who was carrying out road closure duties but is believed to have fled by riding against the flow of traffic before crashing into two marathon participants," he said in a statement today.
He said a 50-year-old woman suffered neck injuries and was receiving treatment at Prince Court, while a 41-year-old man sustained injuries to his right knee and hand.
Zamzuri said the rider and pillion passenger were later taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital for blood and urine samples to facilitate further investigations.
"The case is being investigated under Section 44(1A)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987 and Section 186 of the Penal Code.
"The rider has been remanded for three days from Oct 3 to Oct 5, while the pillion passenger has been remanded for two days until Oct 4," he said.
Both are being held at the Dang Wangi police station lock-up to assist investigations.
Police urged witnesses or those with information on the incident to contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police detonate three mortar bombs found among scrap metal in Dengkil
Article:
SEPANG: Police detonated three mortar bombs this morning, a day after they were found among scrap metal outside a house in Dengkil.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said the bombs, one measuring 81mm and two measuring 60mm, were destroyed by the police Bomb Disposal Unit at an open construction site in Dengkil about 9.20am.
"The disposal operation was completed about 9.25am in a safe and controlled manner. No untoward incidents were reported," he said in a statement today.
The mortar bombs were
discovered
about 3pm yesterday by a man who was sorting scrap metal from a roll-on roll-off (RoRo) bin outside a house in Kampung Dato Ahmad Razali, Dengkil.
Following the discovery, police were dispatched to the scene and secured the area to ensure public safety.
The Bomb Disposal Unit was called in and confirmed that the objects were mortar bombs before removing them to a safe location for disposal.
Norhizam advised the public not to touch, move or approach objects suspected of containing explosives and to immediately contact the police if they encounter such items.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Senior Citizens Bill to strengthen protection for older Malaysians, says Nancy Shukri
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 3 — The physical and mental well-being of senior citizens will be among the key areas addressed under the Senior Citizens Bill, which is expected to be tabled in the Cabinet soon, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said the bill was being drafted to ensure senior citizens receive adequate protection in various aspects of life, enabling them to enjoy a better quality of life.
“The government already has policies and frameworks in place for senior citizens, and this bill is a follow-up measure to further strengthen their protection.
“The bill specifically focuses on safeguarding senior citizens so that they are protected in all aspects,” she told reporters after officiating the 2026 National-Level Senior Citizens Day celebration at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here today.
Also present was Social Welfare Department (JKM) director-general Datuk Che Murad Sayang RamJanuary
Nancy said the bill reflected the government’s commitment to strengthening support, protection and care systems for senior citizens, ensuring they remain relevant to current needs and future demographic changes in the country.
She added that senior citizens should not be regarded as a burden, but instead valued and encouraged to serve as role models for the younger generation, in line with efforts to strengthen family values.
Commenting on the issue of independent speakers, Nancy said her ministry was ready to cooperate with relevant parties to screen individuals appointed to deliver talks to ensure they had the necessary qualifications and calibre.
“It would not be entirely appropriate for us to take over the responsibility (of conducting the screenings) as the matter comes under the purview of other agencies or ministries. However, we can work together by reminding those organising such talks to ensure that the speakers are of high calibre,” she said.
According to media reports, police received a report on September 26 over an allegation of sexual harassment of a child by a motivational speaker.
Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was lodged at 2.09am and the case was being investigated under Section 12 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. — Bernama

Title: Anwar visits Sepang for F1 GP qualifying round, attends welcome dinner hosted by Bahrain crown prince
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 3 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today attended the Formula One (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix qualifying session at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), where he also inspected preparations and the overall running of the race.
Anwar arrived at the circuit at about 4.50pm and was received by Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Petronas President and Group Chief Executive Officer Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik, SIC Chairman Datin Anita Azrina Abdul Aziz and other dignitaries.
He then proceeded for a 15-minute tour of the Mercedes-AMG Petronas team pit.
Following the session, Anwar attended a welcome dinner hosted by Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Bahrain Prince Salman bin Hamad Al-Khalifa at the paddock.
The F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia began yesterday with the first and second free practice sessions, followed by the third free practice session and qualifying today.
The 56-lap race is scheduled to start at 3pm tomorrow.
The event marks the return of Formula One to Sepang after a nine-year absence, with the circuit last hosting an F1 race in 2017.
In July, Formula 1 and the International Automobile Federation (FIA) confirmed that Malaysia would host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement involving F1, the FIA and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The arrangement enables the Bahrain Grand Prix to remain on the 2026 F1 calendar after the original event could not proceed in Bahrain, with the race relocated to Sepang amid the situation in West Asia.
The return of Formula One to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and King Hamad bin Isa Al-Khalifa of Bahrain, as well as the two governments.
Formula One made its debut at Sepang in 1999, with the circuit hosting the Malaysian Grand Prix until 2017. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia aims for economic resilience over efficiency amid global uncertainties, says Tengku Zafrul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Malaysia’s economic focus has shifted from pursuing efficiency to building greater resilience as the country continues to outperform growth forecasts despite global uncertainty, the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) said.
Mida chairman Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz said economic leadership also meant preparing Malaysia to seize clear opportunities while remaining resilient to unpredictable shocks.
He said key fiscal reforms, including fuel subsidy rationalisation and the Fiscal Responsibility Act, had strengthened Malaysia’s public finances.
“But economic reform must be matched by compassion; we must safeguard the vulnerable while building national capacity.
“We must proactively lift incomes by ensuring wages rise alongside productivity, creating higher-paying jobs and boosting entrepreneurship,” he said in his special leadership address at the Youth Economic Forum here today.
The former Investment, Trade and Industry Minister said trade routes were being redrawn while artificial intelligence (AI) was both empowering and disrupting the workforce, reshaping jobs that had once provided young people with their first foothold in a career.
Tengku Zafrul said Malaysia’s young population could become an economic dividend only if it translated into higher productivity, innovation, high-value jobs and new businesses.
“As record investment flows into our region and our country, we must keep asking: what does this investment create for Malaysians? How many high-income jobs? How many young engineers with new skills? How many small and medium-sized enterprises plugged into global supply chains?
“Capital should build stronger firms, and technology should build better skills,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Anwar calls on young Malaysians to master AI and new tech to drive economic growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged Malaysia’s youth to master emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing to drive economic growth.
He said young people must be prepared to explore new fields of knowledge to ensure the country’s technological advancement is guided by its own values, ethics and principles.
“Digital transformation requires AI. Otherwise, we will fall behind in development and in our ability to strengthen the economy.
“I said recently in Shanghai, when I was with Chinese Premier (Li Qiang), that we must master AI. Otherwise, AI will master us,” he said.
Anwar was speaking at the opening of the Youth Economic Forum 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre today.
Also present were Youth and Sports Minister Mohammed Taufiq Johari, political secretary to the finance minister Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim, Perdana Fellows Alumni Association president Fanitsyara Kam Phon, and Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
Anwar said while digital transformation and high-technology economic development were essential, such progress should not come at the expense of ethics, morality and human values.
“Reach for the skies, but remain rooted in the ground. That means new technology, new sciences, new research ... but do not let AI erode moral, ethical and human values,” he said.
Anwar said the government would continue to improve the quality of education, strengthen proficiency in Bahasa Melayu and English, and give young Malaysians opportunities to master other languages, including Chinese, Tamil, Arabic, French and German.
He also urged young people to exercise critical thinking and not become “tools” or blindly devoted to any particular individual or political party.
Instead, he urged the younger generation to be devoted to truth, justice, the pursuit of knowledge and integrity as they work to lead the country towards greater success.
“I am confident that if this is the new spirit, we will see our country move forward at speed and, within 10 years, we will no longer recognise the Malaysia of today. Instead, we will see a new, vibrant, progressive and successful Malaysia,” he said. — Bernama

Title: PAS leaders missed Dr Hasmah’s funeral due to prior commitments, says Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said most PAS leaders could not attend Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali’s funeral because they had prior commitments at home and abroad.
The party’s deputy president said PAS had conveyed its condolences directly to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his family, according to
Sinar Harian
.
“We acknowledge that most PAS leaders had specific programmes on the day she passed away,” he said at a press conference for the Zulkifli Muhammad Islamic Studies Convocation Ceremony (KUIZM) in Gombak today.
Tuan Ibrahim, who is also Perikatan Nasional’s Pahang chairman, said the absence was not deliberate.
He cited his own involvement in a programme in Kelantan, along with Secretary-General Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Vice-President Datuk Mohd Amar Abdullah.
“Thus, their absence was indeed due to unavoidable programmes,” he said.
PAS sent Muslimat wing chief and Central Committee member Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim, and joined the tahlil at Dr Mahathir’s home, he said.
Tuan Ibrahim said Dr Hasmah’s death is unexpected and her burial must be expedited without waiting for anyone.
“Sometimes a father dies but the child cannot make it in time because the death was sudden,” he said.
“We cannot wait long because when someone dies, the body must be buried quickly.”
He said the party had conveyed its condolences on behalf of PAS.
“May he (Dr Mahathir) be patient with what has happened, and what matters is that we pray that the soul of the late Dr Hasmah be blessed and placed among the righteous servants of Allah,” he said.
Dr Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) at 9.20am on September 28, as reported by Sinar Harian.
Her son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir, confirmed the news of the passing of the 100-year-old.
Dr Hasmah was born on July 12, 1926, and married Tun Dr Mahathir on August 5, 1956.

Title: ‘Will my job still exist in 10 years’ time?’: Ahead of Budget 2027, youth minister sums up young Malaysians’ fears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Malaysian youths today have three main concerns, including whether their existing jobs would still exist in the next decade, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said today.
Speaking at the Perdana Fellows Alumni Association’s (PFAA) Youth Economic Forum 2026 (YEF 2026), Dr Taufiq said his ministry had been part of a Budget roadshow in six zones nationwide to engage with youths ahead of the government’s upcoming Budget 2027.
He noted that the youths did not ask theoretical questions, and summarised their questions as revolving around three main concerns.
“Firstly, can youths bear the cost of living?
“Secondly, will my job today still exist 10 years from now? And the third question that is frequently mentioned by youths, if I fall, who will help me?” he said ahead of the tabling of the government’s Budget 2027 in Parliament next Friday.
Dr Taufiq said the panel discussions at today’s YEF on artificial intelligence, talent, green energy and social protection would answer these questions, as youths would not feel the benefits of government policies if those policies fail to address their anxieties.
While saying that youths are often told to be strong and to upskill themselves, Dr Taufiq said that being strong or resilient is not a policy.
“Being strong is what the public is forced to do temporarily while they wait for policies to come. Our duty is to create a protection system that is strong enough so that Malaysia’s youths do not have to ‘bersusah payah’ (toil) to be heroes just to continue living,” he said.
He added that the federal government is currently working on raising both the ceiling and the floor of the economy to ensure that all citizens feel the benefits from foreign direct investments into Malaysia.
He thanked the youths for their proposals on developing the country, and expressed hope that they could also help build the nation together.
At the YEF 2026, which carried the theme of “Decoding the Next Decade: Advancing Malaysia’s Economic Frontier”, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim received six policy proposals that the PFAA had developed based on a nationwide survey of more than 2,000 youths.
The six proposals covered artificial intelligence (AI), green entrepreneurship, skills development, better public services, foreign direct investment, and establishing a National Youth Economic Action Council to give youths a permanent platform to make economic policies.
Anwar also received a memorandum on the youths’ proposals for Budget 2027 at the forum.
